root_cause: Read-only specialist lane (oracle) tasked with producing a deliverable JSON payload that must persist to disk; no persistence plan at dispatch time; orchestrator assumed the payload would survive in the lane's ephemeral response buffer.
corrective_action: When dispatching a write-required deliverable to a read-only lane, either (a) require the full payload inside the returned task result text, or (b) have the lane write to a permitted path, or (c) if neither is possible, dispatch a write-capable lane (fixer). Verify payload capture BEFORE lane close.
verification: Validated on TICKET-005 regeneration: ora-5 was instructed to persist JSON to %TEMP%\opencode\l4_antihypertensive.json; payload persisted and merged into api/drugs.json (49/49 drugs), schema-validated, spot-check APPROVE.
closure_evidence: Prevention rule documented in qms/process-mappings.md (Dispatch Persistence Rule, section 1): full payload in task result, OR permitted disk path, OR write-capable lane; verify payload capture BEFORE lane close.
Rule cross-linked to NCR-2026-014 and this CAPA in the traceability table (status CLOSED).
Effectiveness demonstrated during TICKET-005: ora-5 (read-only lane) delivered its 27-drug payload to a permitted disk path on instruction; merge verified 49/49, schema 88/88, spot-check APPROVE.
prevention: Add to orchestrator dispatch checklist: 'If the deliverable must survive the lane, specify persistence mechanism (disk path or full payload in result) at dispatch time.' Documented in qms/process-mappings.md.
